title: Incident Response in IT and OT
subtitle: Nine cards on how enterprises handle a cyber incident, and what changes when the systems run a factory.

cards.headline: Every incident is handled twice: once in the network, once in the room.
cards.body: Technical containment is half the job. The other half is decisions under pressure: who to tell, what to shut down, what to keep as evidence.

cards.headline: Six phases you will keep coming back to
It takes a commander, analysts, lawyers and the plant floor
cards.body: SOC analysts read the SIEM and EDR, legal watches the notification clocks, executives decide on the ransom, engineers keep the process safe.

cards.headline: The first 24 hours are a chain of decisions
cards.body: A ransomware outbreak spreads while you read this. Triage, isolate, preserve evidence, brief the board, call the regulator. Each choice explained, whichever you pick.

cards.headline: In a plant, safety comes before containment
cards.body: A process misbehaves at 2 a.m. Sensor fault, human error or intrusion? Pulling the plug can be the most dangerous move. Investigate the safe way.

cards.headline: Notification clocks

number.label: a common deadline to tell a regulator, counted from when you became aware

cards.body: Play with alert volume, detection time, containment speed and recovery bottlenecks to see what moves damage.

quote.text: Rebuilding the server fixes today. Imaging it first is what lets you explain today in six months.
